name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle, no more than three wheels on the ground, and a motor that displaces 250 cc or less, other than a motorized bicycle. The statute sets the line between it and a motorcycle by displacement alone; an electric motor displaces nothing, so by the statute's text an electric motorcycle is one whatever its power.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground

Its motor displaces 250 cc or less; the statute gives no electric equivalent, but an electric motor has no displacement to exceed it, and the statute sets no power or speed limit, so a road electric motorcycle is one whatever its power
An electric moped without pedals is one too: a bicycle is designed to be pedaled, so it can't be a motorized bicycle
Riders need a motorcycle operator's license (Class M, 16 or older), earned with a written exam, a vision test and a road test, which an MSF rider course within 90 days waives
Riders aged 14 or 15 may instead hold a Class MD motor-driven cycle license, which expires on their 16th birthday
Can't be sold to anyone under 16 who doesn't hold a license to ride it
Riders and passengers under 21 must wear protective headgear, and every rider and passenger must wear protective glasses, goggles or a transparent face shield
Carries a passenger only on a sidecar or an extra seat with footrests, and a rider under 16 can't carry one
Needs a headlight, a rear red reflector and red tail lamp, brakes, a horn, a muffler and electric turn signals
Registered yearly with the Department of Finance and Administration, carries a license plate, and must carry liability insurance
One designed or manufactured exclusively for competition or off-road use isn't required to be registered
These rules don't apply when ridden on a farm or on private property
